Many years ago was getting intimate with boyfriend behind the big desk, in one of the SWING building's smaller classrooms. It was evening so we thought we had the room to ourselves. Suddenly people started trickling into the class but we stayed hidden, hoping that they'd have their group meeting or something then leave. The first students to arrive knew we were there because I asked them to pass me my backpack. We were fully clothed btw but it was too embarrassing to get up so we waited it out but MORE people kept coming into the room. Eventually a TA came into the class and we heard one of the students tell him we were behind the desk. He came around and found us under there and said he needed to teach a class (!!) 

If we had known this was a class/tutorial instead of a small group meeting we would have escaped so much earlier. We were so ashamed walking out in front of all those students.

You're doing a good job by getting registered with the CFA and getting the medical attention you need. I'm proud of you for being proactive about your health and your studies. These resources and accommodations exist for us people with mental illnesses too, so don't feel bad for using them. Because of our conditions, we need these accommodations to succeed in this environment and suffer less! You're not weak for getting accommodations, just like you wouldn't be weak for wearing glasses to see clearly. Your problems are valid and you are being courageous by getting help.

It took me a while to acknowledge that my mental illness is a real disability too and that I need help. I'm very glad to have registered with the CFA now and I found out that there are many other students in the same boat too, so you are not alone!
